results.question: What is a common action a UE must take if an attach request for emergency bearer services is rejected by the network with an EMM cause other than #5 or #35?
results.reference: Upon receiving an ATTACH REJECT message for emergency bearer services with an EMM cause value other than #5, the UE shall perform the actions as described in clause 5.5.1.2.5 and inform the upper layers of the failure of the procedure. This can result in the upper layers requesting establishment of a CS emergency call or other implementation specific mechanisms.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.2.5A, Attach for emergency bearer services not accepted by the network; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.2.5C, Attach for access to RLOS not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: The UE shall not treat this as a permanent rejection; it shall consider the attach attempt for emergency bearer services as failed but may automatically initiate the attach procedure for emergency bearer services again, without requiring user interaction, subject to the applicable timers/restrictions. It shall not set the USIM/UE as attach-not-allowed and shall not update any 'EMM cause value' based restriction lists for emergency services.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.5 (Abnormal cases in the UE, EMM-REGISTERED-INITIATED, Attach for emergency bearer services)

results.question: Which message does a UE send to the network to indicate that a GUTI reallocation has taken place, and which message from the network triggers this reallocation?
results.reference: The UE sends the GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE message to indicate that reallocation of a GUTI has taken place. This is triggered by the network sending the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message to reallocate a GUTI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.17, GUTI reallocation complete; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.16.1, Message definition
results.model_answer: The UE sends a GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE message to the network to indicate that GUTI reallocation has taken place. This is triggered by the network sending a GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message to the UE, which contains the new GUTI (and optionally a new TAI list).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Section 5.4.1 (GUTI reallocation procedure), specifically 5.4.1.2 (GUTI reallocation initiation) and 5.4.1.3 (GUTI reallocation completion)

results.question: If a UE in CS/PS mode 1 or 2 is already attached to both EPS and non-EPS services and needs to detach only from non-EPS services, what procedure must it use and what is the resulting EMM substate?
results.reference: The UE must perform a combined detach procedure for non-EPS services only (detach type 'IMSI detach'). This results in the UE entering the EMM-REGISTERED.IMSI-DETACH-INITIATED substate.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.5, Coordination between EMM and MM; TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.4.9, EMM-REGISTERED.IMSI-DETACH-INITIATED
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate a combined EPS detach procedure by sending a DETACH REQUEST message with Detach Type IE indicating 'combined EPS/IMSI detach' but with switch off not required, requesting detach from non-EPS services only (i.e., IMSI detach). After the network confirms, the UE remains attached for EPS services only and enters EMM-REGISTERED with EMM-CONNECTED or EMM-IDLE substate 'EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE' but marked as attached for EPS services only (not attached for non-EPS services).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.2 (Combined EPS detach procedure) and clause 5.5.2.2.4

results.question: Which clauses state that no abnormal cases have been identified on the network side for their respective procedures?
results.reference: Clause 6.6.3.6 states 'No abnormal cases have been identified'. Clause 6.6.4.5 states 'Apart from the case described in clause 6.3.4, no other abnormal cases have been identified'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.6, Abnormal cases on the network side; TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.4.5, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, the sub-clauses covering the network-side abnormal cases for the GUTI reallocation procedure and the Identification procedure both state that 'No abnormal cases have been identified' for the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clauses 5.4.1.5 (GUTI reallocation procedure – Abnormal cases on the network side) and 5.4.4.5 (Identification procedure – Abnormal cases on the network side)

results.question: If a UE receives an EMM message that is too short to contain a complete message type IE, and this message also contains an out-of-sequence IE that is not encoded as 'comprehension required', how should the UE handle the message and the IE?
results.reference: The message shall be ignored because it is too short. Furthermore, the out-of-sequence IE that is not encoded as 'comprehension required' shall also be ignored.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.2, Message too short; TS 24.301, Clause 7.6.2, Out of sequence IEs
results.model_answer: If the message is too short to contain a complete message type IE, the UE shall discard the message without further processing, regardless of the presence or encoding of any other IE (including out-of-sequence, non-comprehension-required IEs). The check for message length/message type takes precedence, so the out-of-sequence IE handling procedure is never reached in this case.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 7.7 (Handling of unknown, unforeseen, and erroneous protocol data), specifically the sub-clause on 'Message too short to contain a complete message type information element'.

results.question: When the network includes a Back-off timer value IE in a response where the ESM cause is #26 "insufficient resources", under what condition is it also permitted to include the Re-attempt indicator IE?
results.reference: The network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE only if the ESM cause value is not #26 "insufficient resources" when the Back-off timer value IE is included. Since the cause is #26, the Re-attempt indicator IE cannot be included based on this condition.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.19.3, Back-off timer value; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.19.4, Re-attempt indicator
results.model_answer: The Re-attempt indicator IE may be included together with the Back-off timer value IE only if the back-off timer value provided is neither zero nor deactivated, i.e., the network includes the Re-attempt indicator only when it also sets a running (non-zero) back-off timer for that APN/PDN connection or procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.6 / 6.5.4 (ESM cause #26 handling and Re-attempt indicator IE usage with Back-off timer value IE)

results.question: Under what condition would the network include the 'Additional update result' IE in an ATTACH ACCEPT message, and what specific success scenario does it indicate?
results.reference: The network may include the 'Additional update result' IE to provide the UE with additional information about the result of a combined attach procedure if the procedure was successful for EPS services and non-EPS services, or for EPS services and 'SMS only'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.11, Additional update result; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The network includes the 'Additional update result' IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message when the UE has set the 'Additional update type' (AUT) IE with the SMS only bit set to 1 in the ATTACH REQUEST message, indicating the UE is requesting combined attach for SMS service only (i.e., the UE wants to attach for EPS services and be registered for SMS over NAS without needing full CS fallback capability). The network includes 'Additional update result' set to 'SMS only' to indicate that the combined attach was successful for EPS services and the UE is registered for SMS only, meaning no CS fallback registration was performed but SMS delivery via NAS signaling is supported.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Section 5.5.1.2.4 (Attach accepted by the network) and Table 9.9.3.0B.1 (Additional update result information element)

results.question: A UE operating in PS mode 1 changes its configuration regarding the use of SMS to 'SMS service is not preferred to be invoked over IP networks'. What procedure must the UE execute?
results.reference: The UE must transit from PS mode 1 to CS/PS mode 1 and perform a combined tracking area update with IMSI attach (with or without 'SMS only').
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.2.5, Change of configuration regarding the use of SMS.; TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate a Tracking Area Update procedure to update the network with the new MS network feature support IE indicating the SMS availability configuration change.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.1

results.question: A UE that supports A/Gb mode performs an inter-system change from A/Gb mode to S1 mode in EMM-IDLE mode, and its TIN is set to 'P-TMSI'. Which two IEs must the UE include in its TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message?
results.reference: The UE must include the 'GPRS ciphering key sequence number' IE and the 'NonceUE' IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.3, GPRS ciphering key sequence number; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.6, NonceUE
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the old P-TMSI and old routing area identification (RAI) mapped into the EPS old GUTI and old TAI IEs; specifically, the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST shall contain the 'Old GUTI' IE (mapped from P-TMSI and RAI) and the 'Old P-TMSI Signature' IE.

results.question: During a tracking area update procedure, which message from the network provides the UE with EPS mobility management data, and under what condition does the UE respond with a TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE?
results.reference: The network sends the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message to provide the UE with EPS mobility management related data. The UE responds with a TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message if a GUTI has been changed or a new TMSI has been assigned in the accept message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.1, Message definition; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.27, Tracking area update complete
results.model_answer: The network provides EPS mobility management data to the UE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message. The UE responds with TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE only if the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message contained a new GUTI; the UE returns this message to acknowledge receipt of the new GUTI.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Section 5.5.3.2.4 (Tracking area updating procedure accepted by the network)

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include the Mobile station classmark 2 IE during an attach procedure, and under what conditions must it include the Mobile station classmark 3 IE?
results.reference: The UE shall include the Mobile station classmark 2 IE (Clause_8_2_4_9) if it supports SRVCC to GERAN or UTRAN or supports vSRVCC to UTRAN, or if it is performing a combined attach procedure. The UE shall include the Mobile station classmark 3 IE (Clause_8_2_4_10) if it supports SRVCC to GERAN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.9, Mobile station classmark 2; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.10, Mobile station classmark 3
results.model_answer: During the attach procedure, the UE shall include the Mobile Station Classmark 2 IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message if it supports CS Fallback (CSFB) and/or SMS over SGs, i.e., if it supports A/Gb mode or Iu mode. The UE shall include the Mobile Station Classmark 3 IE if it supports CS Fallback and/or SMS over SGs and it supports A/Gb mode, and the Mobile Station Classmark 3 IE contains information (e.g., radio capabilities) required for A/Gb mode operation that is not included in Classmark 2.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Section 5.5.1.2.2 (Attach procedure initiation) and Table 9.9.3.x (Mobile station classmark 2/3 IE description)

results.question: What are the conditions for the network to include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE, and what is the corresponding condition for the UE to include the Requested WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The network shall include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE (Clause_8_2_1_24) if the UE supports WUS assistance, the MME supports and accepts its use, and the UE is not attaching for emergency bearer services. Correspondingly, the UE may include the Requested WUS assistance information IE (Clause_8_2_4_26) if it supports WUS assistance and is not attaching for emergency bearer services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.24, Negotiated WUS assistance information; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.26, Requested WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: The network includes the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message only if the UE included the Requested WUS assistance information IE in the corresponding ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message, and the network supports and decides to negotiate WUS assistance information. The UE includes the Requested WUS assistance information IE in the ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message if the UE supports WUS (Wake Up Signal) and wants to provide WUS assistance information to the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.1.2.2 and 5.5.3.2.4 (Attach/TAU procedures - WUS assistance information IE handling)

results.question: During the ESM information request procedure, what action does the network take regarding protocol configuration options received in an ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message?
results.reference: Upon receipt of the ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message, the network stops timer T3489 and enters the state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE. Furthermore, a protocol configuration options IE or extended protocol configuration options IE included in this message replaces any protocol configuration options IE or extended protocol configuration options IE that the network previously may have received during the attach procedure execution.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.1.2.4, ESM information request completion by the network; TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.1.1, General
results.model_answer: The network takes the received protocol configuration options (PCO) received in the ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message into account, e.g., for forwarding relevant information (such as P-CSCF address requests, DNS server requests, etc.) to the PDN GW during the PDN connectivity procedure, so that the PCO content can be used when establishing the PDN connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.2.3 (ESM information request procedure)

results.question: A UE operating in CS/PS mode 1 changes its voice domain preference for E-UTRAN to 'IMS PS voice only'. It is configured to prefer SMS over IP networks and is available for voice calls in the IMS. According to the procedures, what actions must the UE take?
results.reference: The UE must transit from CS/PS mode 1 to PS mode 1 and perform a detach for non-EPS services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.2.3, Change of voice domain preference for E-UTRAN; TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE shall set the SMS availability indicator to 'UE is available for SMS over IP' and shall send an ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message with the SMS availability indicator IE included, indicating this change to the network, without triggering a new attach or tracking area updating procedure solely for this purpose; the indication is piggybacked on the next occurring mobility management signalling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.3.5.4 (SMS over IP handling) and 5.5.1/5.5.3 (Attach/TAU procedures)

results.question: When is the 'SMS services status' IE included in a tracking area updating procedure, and what does its inclusion signify about the procedure's outcome?
results.reference: The 'SMS services status' IE may be included when a normal tracking area updating procedure for EPS services and 'SMS only' was successful for EPS services only.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.19, SMS services status; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The 'SMS services status' IE is included by the network in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message when combined TA/LA updating with IMSI attach (or combined TA/LA update) was requested and the MME needs to indicate that SMS-over-NAS (SMS services) are restricted or not allowed, even though the tracking area updating (and combined attach for EPS services) itself was accepted. Its presence therefore signifies that the overall TAU procedure succeeded for EPS mobility management, but SMS service availability via the non-EPS/combined domain is limited (e.g., 'SMS not allowed' or a specific restriction cause), rather than indicating failure of the TAU procedure itself.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.4B (SMS services status IE) and clause 5.5.3.2.4 (Tracking area updating procedure accepted by the network)

results.question: For a UE in WB-S1 mode requesting a PDN connection that is not for UAS services and with a PDN Type other than non-IP/Ethernet, which IE related to protocol configuration options should be included if the UE wishes to transmit data to the network and end-to-end ePCO support is not present?
results.reference: The Protocol Configuration Options IE (Clause_8_3_20_4) shall be included. This clause explicitly states the inclusion conditions for this scenario (UE in WB-S1 mode, PDN Type not non-IP/Ethernet, APN not for UAS services). It also states this IE shall not be included if the Extended Protocol Configuration Options IE is included, which aligns with the general rule in Clause_6_6_1_1 that the ePCO IE is used only when there is end-to-end support.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.20.4, Protocol configuration options; TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.1.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the Protocol Configuration Options (PCO) IE (not ePCO) in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, since extended PCO cannot be used when end-to-end ePCO support is not indicated/present.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2

results.question: When must a UE include the Additional information requested IE, and when will the network respond with the Ciphering key data IE?
results.reference: The UE shall include the Additional information requested IE (Clause_8_2_4_23) if it supports ciphered broadcast assistance data and needs to obtain new ciphering keys for it. The network will include the Ciphering key data IE (Clause_8_2_1_21) if it needs to send ciphering key data to the UE for ciphered broadcast assistance data.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.23, Additional information requested; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.21, Ciphering key data
results.model_answer: The UE includes the Additional information requested IE in an EMM message (e.g., in the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, or via a NAS message used to request the deletion of a mismatched CIPHERING KEY DATA IE) when it needs to request ciphering keys for use with unauthenticated emergency calls or when it detects that a previously stored Ciphering Key Data IE is no longer valid (e.g., due to expiry or mismatch) and wants the network to provide new or updated ciphering key data. The network, upon receiving this indication and if it supports and is configured to provide ciphering keys for unauthenticated emergency sessions, responds by including the Ciphering Key Data IE in the corresponding EMM response message (e.g., SERVICE ACCEPT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT, or SECURITY MODE COMMAND) containing the ciphering key(s), associated key index, validity period, and applicable PLMN/tracking area identifiers.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.1 and 9.9.3.62 (Ciphering Key Data IE) and 9.9.3.65 (Additional information requested IE)

results.question: According to the specifications, under what conditions is the Extended Protocol Configuration Options IE used instead of the Protocol Configuration Options IE for exchanging data between the UE and the network?
results.reference: The Extended Protocol Configuration Options IE is used if it is supported by both the UE and the network end-to-end for the PDN connection. Otherwise, the Protocol Configuration Options IE is used. This rule is defined in clause 6.6.1.1 and is referenced by numerous individual IE definitions, such as those in Clause_8_3_1_2 and Clause_8_3_1_4, which specify the use of the PCO or ePCO IEs based on this end-to-end support condition.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.1.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.2, Protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The Extended Protocol Configuration Options (ePCO) IE is used instead of the Protocol Configuration Options (PCO) IE when both the UE and the network support ePCO, and this support has been indicated to each other during the relevant NAS procedure (e.g., PDN connectivity or bearer resource procedures). Specifically, the UE indicates support for ePCO in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, and the network indicates support for ePCO to the UE. If both support it, ePCO is used for exchanging protocol configuration data (e.g., DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses) instead of PCO, since ePCO allows larger container sizes than PCO.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.4.26 (Extended protocol configuration options) and Clause 6.5.1.2 (indication of support for extended protocol configuration options during PDN connectivity procedures)

results.question: According to the specifications, what are the two optional IEs related to network naming that can be provided to the UE?
results.reference: The two optional IEs are: one to assign a new full name for network (Clause 8.2.19.7) and one to assign a new short name for network (Clause 8.2.19.8).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.7, Full name for network; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.8, Short name for network
results.model_answer: Network name and Short network name
results.evidence: TS 24.501, EMM INFORMATION message, clause 8.2.13 (Information Elements: 'Full name for network' and 'Short name for network')

results.question: Which IEs can be included to assign a new TAI list to the UE?
results.reference: The TAI list IE may be included to assign a TAI list to a UE (Clause_8_2_7_4). The TAI list IE may also be included to assign a new TAI list to the UE (Clause_8_2_19_4).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.4, TAI list; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.4, TAI list
results.model_answer: The Tracking Area Identity List IE is included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message to assign a new TAI list to the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.7 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT) - Tracking area identity list IE

results.question: According to the specifications, when a UE has a valid 5G NAS security context and needs to send non-cleartext IEs in a REGISTRATION REQUEST message, how should the message be protected?
results.reference: The UE includes the entire REGISTRATION REQUEST message (i.e. containing both cleartext IEs and non-cleartext IEs) in the NAS message container IE, ciphers the value part of the NAS message container IE, and then sends a REGISTRATION REQUEST message containing the cleartext IEs and the NAS message container IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.6, Protection of initial NAS signalling messages; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.21, NAS message container
results.model_answer: The UE shall send the REGISTRATION REQUEST message integrity protected (and if a valid context supporting ciphering exists, also ciphered) using the current 5G NAS security context. The non-cleartext IEs are included in a separate NAS message container IE which is ciphered, while the REGISTRATION REQUEST message itself is sent integrity protected within a security-protected NAS message.

results.question: When the AMF includes the Back-off timer value IE in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message, what specific condition related to the Payload container must be met, and what is the general purpose of the network-initiated NAS transport procedure that uses this message?
results.reference: The AMF includes the Back-off timer value IE when the Payload container IE contains an uplink 5GSM message which was not forwarded due to specified congestion or subscription issues, and the Payload container type IE is not set to 'Multiple payloads'. The purpose of the network-initiated NAS transport procedure is to provide transport of various payload types, including such non-forwarded 5GSM messages, from the AMF to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.11.5, Back-off timer value; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.5.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The AMF includes the Back-off timer value IE in the DL NAS TRANSPORT message only when the Payload container type IE indicates that the Payload container IE contains an SMS payload (i.e., SMS is being transported). The general purpose of the network-initiated NAS transport procedure using DL NAS TRANSPORT is to allow the AMF to carry, in a NAS message, payloads such as SMS, LPP messages, UE policy information, or other data that need to be transferred transparently to the UE without requiring interpretation by the AMF.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.5.2.3 (Network-initiated NAS transport procedure) and clause 8.2.10 (DL NAS TRANSPORT message)

results.question: Which clause specifies a capability related to UAV flight authorization, and which clause specifies an IE inclusion based on operator policy?
results.reference: Clause 4.22.4 states that the 5GS supports USS authorization of UAV flight. Clause 8.2.7.23 states that the NSSAI inclusion mode IE shall be included if required by operator policy.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.22.4, Authorization of UAV flight; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.23, NSSAI inclusion mode
results.model_answer: Clause 5.4.4a (UAS/UUAA-related procedures) specifies the capability related to UAV flight authorization, handled via the UAS Aerial UE indication/UUAA procedure. Clause 9.11.3.18A (or the relevant IE description clause, e.g., 5.5.1.2.4) specifies IE inclusion based on operator policy, where the network includes certain IEs in NAS messages depending on operator configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.4a (UUAA procedure) and Clause 9.11.3.18A (IE inclusion based on operator policy)

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include both the Mobile station classmark 2 and Supported codecs IEs?
results.reference: Both IEs shall be included if the UE supports 5G-SRVCC from NG-RAN to UTRAN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.25, Mobile station classmark 2; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.26, Supported codecs
results.model_answer: The UE shall include both the Mobile Station Classmark 2 IE and the Supported Codec List IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message if the UE supports voice calls (e.g., IMS voice over PS or CS fallback) and the message is sent over 3GPP access, so that the network can determine the UE's voice capabilities for setting up services such as SRVCC or CS fallback.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.1 (Registration request), description of the Mobile station classmark 2 and Supported codecs IEs in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.

results.question: According to the clauses, what are the two main purposes of the de-registration procedure when initiated by the UE?
results.reference: The de-registration procedure is used by the UE to de-register for 5GS services over 3GPP access when the UE is registered over 3GPP access, and to de-register for 5GS services over non-3GPP access when the UE is registered over non-3GPP access.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.2.3, UE-initiated de-registration procedure completion for 5GS services over 3GPP access
results.model_answer: The UE-initiated de-registration procedure is used (1) to de-register from one or more access types (3GPP access, non-3GPP access, or both) for a given PLMN with the network, and (2) to inform the network that the UE wants to switch off, enabling the network to release resources and context associated with that UE without waiting for other triggers (e.g., timer expiry).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2 (De-registration procedure initiated by the UE)

results.question: What must a UE do to request the use of MICO mode, and under what conditions must the network include the MICO indication IE in response?
results.reference: The UE may include the MICO indication IE to request the use of MICO mode. The network shall include the MICO indication IE if the UE included the MICO indication IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message and the network supports and accepts the use of MICO mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.10, MICO indication; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.13, MICO indication
results.model_answer: To request MICO (Mobile Initiated Connection Only) mode, the UE shall include the MICO indication IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message during an initial registration or mobility/periodic registration update procedure. The network (AMF) shall include the MICO indication IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message only if the UE requested MICO mode and the network accepts the use of MICO mode for the UE; if the network does not support or does not accept MICO mode, it shall not include the MICO indication IE, in which case the UE shall consider that MICO mode is not used.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1 (Registration procedure) and clause 5.4.1a (MICO mode)

results.question: If a UE wants to use or change its UE-specific DRX parameters, what must it include in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message? What is the corresponding condition for the network to include the Negotiated DRX parameters IE?
results.reference: If the UE wants to use or change the UE specific DRX parameters, the UE shall include the Requested DRX parameters IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message. The network shall include the Negotiated DRX parameters IE if the Requested DRX parameters IE was included in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.15, Requested DRX parameters; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.25, Negotiated DRX parameters
results.model_answer: The UE must include the Requested DRX parameters IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message, indicating the UE-specific DRX parameter value it wants to use. If the network accepts the use of UE-specific DRX parameters, it shall include the Negotiated DRX parameters IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message with the negotiated value, which may differ from the requested value.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.2 and 5.5.1.3.2 (Registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update, and initial registration - UE-specific DRX parameters negotiation)

results.question: In which procedures can the network provision a 'CAG information list' to the UE, and what is a key purpose of this list in the context of PNI-NPN access?
results.reference: The network can provision a 'CAG information list' to the UE via the generic UE configuration update procedure, the registration procedure, the service request procedure, and the network-initiated de-registration procedure (Clause_4_14_3). A key purpose of this list in PNI-NPN is to prevent UEs not allowed to access a PNI-NPN from accessing it (Clause_4_14_3).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.14.3, Public network integrated non-public network (PNI-NPN); TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.36, CAG information list
results.model_answer: The network can provision the 'CAG information list' to the UE during the Registration procedure and the Generic UE configuration update procedure. A key purpose of this list, in the context of PNI-NPN (Public Network Integrated NPN) access, is to inform the UE which CAG (Closed Access Group) cells/PLMN-CAG ID combinations it is allowed to access, and whether the UE is only allowed to access 5GS via CAG cells, thereby controlling and restricting the UE's cell selection/access to authorized CAG cells of that PNI-NPN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.16.3 (Access control for CAG using CAG information list) and clause 5.5.1 (Registration procedure) / 5.4.4 (Generic UE configuration update procedure)

results.question: Which two IEs can be included to assign new network names to the UE, and what is the distinction between them?
results.reference: The IE in Clause 8.2.19.7 can be included to assign a new full name for network to the UE. The IE in Clause 8.2.19.8 can be included to assign a new short name for network to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.7, Full name for network; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.8, Short name for network
results.model_answer: The two IEs are the 'Network name' (Full name for network) and 'Short network name' IEs. They are both included in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message. The distinction is that the 'Network name' IE provides the full textual name of the network (PLMN) for display purposes, while the 'Short network name' IE provides an abbreviated version of the same network name, intended for display when the UE cannot show the full name (e.g., due to display size constraints).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4.2 (Network identity and time zone update procedure) and clause 8.2.16 (CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message content, IEs 'Full name for network' and 'Short name for network')

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include the Service-level-AA container IE in a message, and which specific messages require it?
results.reference: The UE shall include the Service-level-AA container IE if the UE supporting UAS services requests a registration for UAS services (Clause_8_2_6_35). Furthermore, this IE shall be included in the message when the UE needs to establish a PDU session for the UAS services (Clause_8_3_1_16).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.35, Service-level-AA container; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.16, Service-level-AA container
results.model_answer: The UE must include the Service-level-AA container IE when it needs to convey service-level authentication, authorization or key management (e.g., for PC5, ProSe, or V2X service-level-AA) information to the network, specifically to request or respond to service-level AA procedures with an AA server via the SMF. This IE is included in the UL NAS TRANSPORT message when the UE sends a Service-level-AA payload to the network, and in the DL NAS TRANSPORT message when the network sends a Service-level-AA payload to the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.9 (UL NAS TRANSPORT) and clause 8.2.10 (DL NAS TRANSPORT), Service-level-AA container IE description.

results.question: Which IEs can be included to assign a new service area list to the UE?
results.reference: The Service area list IE may be included to assign new service area restrictions to the UE (Clause_8_2_7_15). The Service area list IE may also be included to assign a new service area list to the UE (Clause_8_2_19_6).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.15, Service area list; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.6, Service area list
results.model_answer: The Service area list IE can be included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message (and also in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message) to assign a new service area list to the UE, indicating allowed and/or non-allowed tracking areas.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.7 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT) and clause 8.2.16 (CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND) – Service area list IE (9.11.3.49)

results.question: In which message can the network send an extended local emergency numbers list for an SNPN, and what specific condition must be met for the 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming"' IE to be included in a message?
results.reference: In case of SNPN, the network may send an extended local emergency numbers list in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message by including the Extended emergency number list IE. The 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming"' IE is included only if the message is sent via satellite NG-RAN access.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.12, Handling of local emergency numbers; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.48, Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming"
results.model_answer: The network can send an extended local emergency numbers list for an SNPN in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message. The 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming"' IE is included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message only if the AMF is including one or more tracking areas as forbidden tracking areas for roaming, i.e., only if there is at least one forbidden TAI for this list to report to the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.7.31 (Extended local emergency numbers list IE) and clause 8.2.7.62 / 9.11.3.53 (Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming" IE) as included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message description, clause 8.2.7 (Registration accept).

results.question: What are two IEs that must be included based on the UE's support for specific voice-related capabilities?
results.reference: The UE's usage setting IE shall be included if the UE supports IMS voice. The Mobile station classmark 2 IE shall be included if the UE supports 5G-SRVCC from NG-RAN to UTRAN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.14, UE's usage setting; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.25, Mobile station classmark 2
results.model_answer: The two IEs are the 5GMM Capability IE (with the S1 mode bit indicating IMS voice over PS session/voice support) and the UE Status/UE Usage Setting or more specifically the 'Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting' IE (or IMS voice over PS session supported indicator), which must be included when the UE supports voice services (e.g., IMS voice over PS or EPS fallback) to allow the network to determine appropriate voice domain selection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.6 (Registration Request) and clause 9.11.3.53 (5GMM Capability IE)

results.question: When a UE camps on a satellite NG-RAN cell and receives multiple TACs, how does it select a TAI if no TAI belongs to its current registration area? What lists does the UE store for forbidden tracking areas when not operating in SNPN access operation mode?
results.reference: If no TAI belongs to the current registration area of the UE and there is a TAI which belongs to neither the list of '5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming' nor the list of '5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service', the UE shall select such a TAI. When not operating in SNPN access operation mode, the UE shall store a list of '5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming', as well as a list of '5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.23.5, Handling multiple tracking area codes from the lower layers; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.13, Lists of 5GS forbidden tracking areas
results.model_answer: If the UE receives multiple TACs on a satellite NG-RAN cell and none of the TAIs (formed from the broadcast PLMN identity and each TAC) belongs to its current registration area, the UE selects the TAI with the lowest TAC value among those broadcast. This selected TAI is then used for registration area management (e.g., to determine if a Registration Update is needed). For forbidden tracking areas, when not operating in SNPN access operation mode, the UE stores two separate lists: (1) the 'list of forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service', and (2) the 'list of forbidden tracking areas for roaming'.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.9.5 (satellite NG-RAN TAC selection) and clause 4.6.2 (forbidden tracking area lists).

results.question: Under what conditions can the AMF initiate a security mode control procedure to change the uplink NAS COUNT used in the latest SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message?
results.reference: The network may initiate the security mode control procedure in order to change the value of uplink NAS COUNT used in the latest SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message as described in 3GPP TS 33.501, subclause 6.9.4.4.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The AMF can initiate a new security mode control procedure to change the uplink NAS COUNT that was used in the latest SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message only if that SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message was sent in response to a SECURITY MODE COMMAND used to take into use new mapped 5G NAS security context (i.e., during inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, when mapping an EPS security context to a 5G NAS security context), and provided that no NAS signalling connection release has occurred since then.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.2.7 (Security mode control procedure - abnormal cases on the network side)

results.question: What information elements may be included to update the UE's network identifiers, and what specific type of name does each provide?
results.reference: Two IEs may be included: one provides a new full name for the network (Clause 8.2.19.7), and the other provides a new short name for the network (Clause 8.2.19.8).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.7, Full name for network; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.8, Short name for network
results.model_answer: The AMF may include the Operator-defined access category definitions IE and the Network name IEs in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT (or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND) message to update UE network identifiers: specifically, the 'Full name for network' IE provides the full textual name of the network/PLMN, and the 'Short name for network' IE provides an abbreviated (short-form) textual name of the network/PLMN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.16 (Configuration update command) / clause 9.11.3.x (Full name for network, Short name for network IEs)

results.question: What are the conditions for including the 5GSM cause IE in a message, and what is a specific example of its use when a UE rejects a network request?
results.reference: The 5GSM cause IE is included in the message to indicate the reason for the deletion of one or more non-default QoS rules, QoS flow descriptions or mapped EPS bearer contexts (Clause_8_3_7_3). A specific example is when a UE rejects a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message; in this case, the UE shall create a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message and set the 5GSM cause IE to indicate the reason for rejecting the PDU session modification (Clause_6_3_2_4).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.3, 5GSM cause; TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.2.4, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The 5GSM cause IE shall be included in a 5GSM message when it is necessary to indicate the reason for a particular 5GSM procedure outcome, especially rejection or failure of a request. It is optional in success messages but mandatory in reject/failure type messages to inform the peer entity why the request could not be accepted. A specific example: when a UE rejects a network-requested PDU session modification (e.g., via the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message), the UE shall include the 5GSM cause IE set to an appropriate value (e.g., #43 'invalid PDU session identity value' or other applicable cause) to indicate the reason for rejecting the network's request to modify the PDU session.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.4.2 and clause 6.4.2.3 (PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT)

results.question: Under what condition is the 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service"' IE included in a message, and what is the UE's behavior regarding the 'extended local emergency numbers list' when receiving a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message via non-3GPP access from a PLMN in a different country?
results.reference: The 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service"' IE is included only if the message is sent via satellite NG-RAN access. When a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message is received via non-3GPP access from a PLMN in a country different from the current country of the UE, the UE shall keep the stored extended local emergency numbers list, if available.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.14.10, Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas forregional provision of service"; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.12, Handling of local emergency numbers
results.model_answer: The 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service"' IE is included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message only if the AMF has TAI(s) to be included in this specific forbidden TAI list for regional provision of service. Regarding the extended local emergency numbers list, if the UE receives a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message via non-3GPP access and the PLMN identity in the 5GS registration result is different from the PLMN identity of the entry (if any) currently stored for 3GPP access, the UE shall not apply the stored extended local emergency numbers list for the non-3GPP access; it shall instead treat any such list received via 3GPP access as valid only for 3GPP access, and shall not use it for non-3GPP access unless explicitly received/applicable for non-3GPP access.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.4 (Registration accept for mobility and periodic registration update) and clause 4.5A (Extended local emergency numbers list handling)

results.question: Which IEs can be included to assign a new 5G-GUTI to the UE?
results.reference: The 5G-GUTI IE may be included to assign a 5G-GUTI to a UE (Clause_8_2_7_2). The 5G-GUTI IE may also be included to assign a new 5G GUTI to the UE (Clause_8_2_19_3).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.2, 5G-GUTI; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.3, 5G-GUTI
results.model_answer: The 5GS mobility management (5GMM) messages used to assign a new 5G-GUTI to the UE include the 5G-GUTI IE itself, typically carried within the Registration Accept message or the Configuration Update Command message, using the IE '5G-GUTI' (IEI populated as per message). Specifically: In Registration Accept, the 5G-GUTI is included as the '5G-GUTI' IE. In Configuration Update Command, the 5G-GUTI is included as the '5G-GUTI' IE as well, often accompanied by the 'TAI list' IE to indicate the new registration area associated with the assigned GUTI.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.7 (Registration Accept) and clause 8.2.16 (Configuration Update Command), specifically the '5G-GUTI' IE definition in clause 9.11.3.4.

results.question: What integrity protection applies when the network provides a Payload container IE with the type set to 'SOR transparent container' in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message, and in which specific NAS message from the UE is the PDU session ID IE mandated when carrying 'N1 SM information'?
results.reference: When the network provides a Payload container IE with the Payload container type IE set to 'SOR transparent container' in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message, the Payload container IE is integrity protected by the HPLMN or subscribed SNPN. The UE shall include the PDU session ID IE in the UL NAS TRANSPORT message when the Payload container type IE is set to 'N1 SM information'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.7, Protection of NAS IEs; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.10.2, PDU session ID
results.model_answer: When the DL NAS TRANSPORT message carries a Payload container IE of type 'SOR transparent container', the message must be sent integrity protected (using the current 5G NAS security context) after a successful primary authentication and key agreement procedure; ciphering is not required, but integrity protection is mandatory (the AMF shall not send this before security context establishment). Regarding the PDU session ID IE carrying 'N1 SM information', it is mandatory in the UL NAS TRANSPORT message sent by the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1a (steering of roaming) and clause 8.2.10.1/Table 8.2.10 (UL NAS TRANSPORT message - PDU session ID IE)

results.question: What is the relationship between mapped EPS bearer contexts and QoS rules in an MA PDU session, and what action does the UE take regarding mapped EPS bearer contexts?
results.reference: In an MA PDU session, the UE shall have one set of the mapped EPS bearer contexts, and the network can provide this set via either access of the MA PDU session (Clause_6_1_4_1). The UE can request to delete one or more mapped EPS bearer contexts by including the Mapped EPS bearer contexts IE in a message (Clause_8_3_7_10).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.4.1, Coordination between 5GSM and ESM with N26 interface; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.10, Mapped EPS bearer contexts
results.model_answer: In an MA PDU session, mapped EPS bearer contexts are derived from the QoS rules and QoS flow descriptions associated with the PDU session, similar to how they are created for a single-access PDU session capable of being handed over to EPS. Each mapped EPS bearer context is linked to the QoS rule(s) and QoS flow description from which it was derived. The UE creates and maintains mapped EPS bearer contexts for the MA PDU session using the same rules as for other PDU sessions (i.e., deriving EPS bearer contexts from the QoS rules/QoS flow descriptions), and it stores them together with the MA PDU session so they can be used if and when the session is handed over to, or additionally uses, EPS via the 3GPP access, consistent with the mapping procedures defined for non-MA PDU sessions.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.2.4 (Mapped EPS bearer contexts) and clause 6.4.9 (Handling of MA PDU sessions in mobility to EPS)

results.question: Under what conditions must the network include the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE in a registration accept message, and what is a key restriction on the UE's use of eDRX?
results.reference: The network shall include the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE if the UE included the Requested extended DRX parameters IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message and the network supports eDRX and accepts the use of eDRX. The UE shall use eDRX only if it received the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE during the last registration procedure and the UE does not have an emergency PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.27, Negotiated extended DRX parameters; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.16, Extended DRX cycle for UEs in 5GMM-IDLE and 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication
results.model_answer: The network includes the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message only if the UE included an Extended DRX parameters IE in its REGISTRATION REQUEST (i.e., the UE requested eDRX) and the network accepts/negotiates the use of eDRX for the UE. If this IE is not included by the network, the UE cannot use eDRX. A key restriction is that the UE is only allowed to use the negotiated eDRX parameters as provided by the network (the UE cannot use eDRX parameters it requested if the network did not return this IE, and the UE must use the value given by the network, which may differ from what it requested), and eDRX cannot be used together with non-discontinuous reception (or with negotiated use of an active time / other conflicting configurations) unless specifically supported.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.4 (Registration accept) – description of the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE inclusion condition and its use.

results.question: Under what condition does a UE transition from the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE substate to the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION substate, and what is the general definition of the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state?
results.reference: A UE transitions from 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION if it receives a request from upper layers to establish an eCall over IMS or a call to an HPLMN designated non-emergency MSISDN/URI for test or terminal reconfiguration service. In the state 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, no 5GMM context has been established or the 5GMM context is marked as deregistered. The UE is deregistered.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.3.7, eCALL-INACTIVE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.3.2, 5GMM-DEREGISTERED
results.model_answer: The UE transitions from 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION when a registration procedure requested by upper layers or for mobility and periodic registration update fails or is aborted (e.g., due to lower layer failure, network rejection with a retry-allowed cause, or other abnormal conditions) and the UE needs to retry registration outside of an eCall inactivity context. In general terms, the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state represents the state in which the UE is not registered with the network; no valid 5GMM context (security or mobility context) is established for the UE at the AMF, and the UE and network 5GMM contexts hold no valid location or routing information for the UE, meaning the UE is not reachable by the network and cannot receive most services until it successfully performs a registration procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.3.2 (5GMM-DEREGISTERED state and substates)

results.question: When does the UE include the 'Extended protocol configuration options' IE, and when does the network include its counterpart?
results.reference: The UE includes the 'Extended protocol configuration options' IE in a message when it needs to transmit (protocol) data (e.g., configuration parameters, error codes) to the network (Clause_8_3_1_9). The network includes the 'Extended protocol configuration options' IE in a message when it needs to transmit (protocol) data to the UE (Clause_8_3_3_5).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.9, Extended protocol configuration options; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.3.5, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The UE includes the Extended protocol configuration options IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST (and may include it in PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST) messages when it needs to transfer information related to a PDU session (e.g. to the DN/PDN, or DNS/P-CSCF addresses, DHCP, etc.) that cannot fit or is not appropriate in the Protocol configuration options IE, or when it needs to send parameters that require the extended IE format (e.g. IPv6 or larger content). The network (SMF) includes the Extended protocol configuration options IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT (and may include it in PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND) messages when it needs to return configuration information (e.g. DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses) to the UE that is associated with the PDU session, using the extended IE format instead of, or in addition to, the legacy Protocol configuration options IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.4.13 (Extended protocol configuration options)

results.question: What are two events that cause a UE to enter the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state, and what is the purpose of the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION substate?
results.reference: Two events that cause a UE to enter the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state are: a) the de-registration is performed either by the UE or by the network, and b) the registration request is rejected by the AMF. The substate 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION is chosen in the UE if the initial registration procedure failed due to a missing response from the network or due to specific error circumstances.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.1.3.4, 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION
results.model_answer: A UE enters the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state upon: (1) successful de-registration (either UE-initiated or network-initiated de-registration procedure completing), and (2) failure of an initial registration procedure (e.g., due to abnormal cases such as lower layer failure, or the registration attempt counter reaching a certain state). The 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION substate is used to represent that the UE is in the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state but is attempting to register (i.e., a registration attempt has failed in a way that allows retry), and it applies specific timers/counters (e.g., T3511/T3502) and restrictions to control retry attempts, ensuring the UE does not repeatedly and immediately attempt registration in an uncontrolled manner while still remaining eligible to reattempt registration when conditions allow.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.3.2 (5GMM-DEREGISTERED state and substates)

results.question: How does the UE determine the RRC establishment cause for non-3GPP access, and what is the role of access identities in this process?
results.reference: When establishment of an N1 NAS signalling connection over non-3GPP access is initiated, the UE shall determine one or more access identities to be associated with the establishment as specified in subclause 4.5.2 and table 4.5.2.1, and then select the establishment cause for non-3GPP access from the determined one or more access identities and the event which triggered the initiation by checking the rules specified in table 4.7.2.2.1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.7.2.2, Establishment cause for non-3GPP access; TS 24.301, Clause 4.5.2, Determination of the access identities and access category associated with a request for access for UEs not operating in SNPN access mode
results.model_answer: For non-3GPP access, the RRC establishment cause concept as used in 3GPP access does not apply, because NAS signalling over non-3GPP access is transported via IPsec/NWu (or trusted WLAN/wireline interworking) to the N3IWF/TNGF/W-AGF and not via RRC. Access identities and their associated establishment causes (used for access control/RRC establishment cause selection, e.g. via access category and access identity mapping per TS 24.501 Annex C and TS 38.331) are only relevant for the 3GPP access RRC connection establishment. Consequently, for non-3GPP access, the UE does not select or include an RRC establishment cause; instead, unified access control (UAC) categorization based on access identities (e.g., MPS, MCS, multimedia priority, or standard access identity 0) applies only when the UE also has or establishes a 3GPP access, and it has no bearing on how the UE connects to non-3GPP access, where connection establishment is governed by the underlying non-3GPP access technology and IKEv2/IPsec procedures rather than RRC establishment cause or access identity-based barring checks.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.1.3 (Access via non-3GPP access) and clause 5.3.1 / Annex C (Unified Access Control) — access identity-based establishment cause selection applies only to RRC/3GPP access, not to non-3GPP access.

results.question: What are the input parameters to the NAS ciphering algorithm when applying initial NAS message protection to a REGISTRATION REQUEST or SERVICE REQUEST message?
results.reference: The input parameters are the BEARER ID, DIRECTION bit, NAS COUNT, NAS encryption key, and the length of the key stream to be generated by the encryption algorithm. The length of the key stream is set to the length of the entire plain NAS message that is included in the NAS message container IE, i.e., the value part of the NAS message container IE, that is to be ciphered.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.3.4, Ciphering and deciphering; TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.6, Protection of initial NAS signalling messages
results.model_answer: For initial NAS message protection of a REGISTRATION REQUEST or SERVICE REQUEST, the UE applies the 5G NAS ciphering algorithm currently in use (as indicated by the ngKSI of the current 5G NAS security context) using: KEY = KNASenc of the current 5G NAS security context; COUNT = NAS COUNT of the current 5G NAS security context (uplink NAS COUNT, with the security header set to 'integrity protected and ciphered with new 5G NAS security context' not used for the initial ciphering, i.e. the value of the current NAS COUNT is used as is); BEARER = the value of the access type (3GPP access or non-3GPP access) as specified for NAS security context usage; DIRECTION = uplink; LENGTH = the length of the plaintext NAS message (i.e. the IEs to be ciphered, such as the payload container containing the REGISTRATION REQUEST or SERVICE REQUEST IEs beyond the ones sent in cleartext).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.4.6 (and Annex C) – Integrity protection and ciphering of initial NAS messages

results.question: Under what two conditions related to disaster scenarios might the network include specific IEs to assign wait ranges to the UE?
results.reference: The network may include the 'Disaster roaming wait range' IE to assign a new disaster roaming wait range to the UE (Clause_8_2_7_45). The network may also include the 'Disaster return wait range' IE to assign a new disaster return wait range to the UE (Clause_8_2_7_46).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.45, Disaster roaming wait range; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.46, Disaster return wait range
results.model_answer: The network may include the Rejected NSSAI IE and/or the Extended rejected NSSAI IE with a specific rejection cause to assign wait ranges to the UE when: (1) the UE requests network slice(s) usable only for disaster roaming service while the UE is not in disaster roaming, or (2) the UE requests normal network slice(s) while the UE is in disaster roaming condition, and the network needs to control/stagger UE re-attempts due to disaster-related congestion.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1 and clause 9.11.3.46 (Rejected NSSAI IE) / 9.11.3.95 (Extended rejected NSSAI IE), disaster roaming related provisions

results.question: Under what condition is the Payload container type IE set to 'UE policy container' in a REGISTRATION REQUEST message, and what is the purpose of the UE-initiated NAS transport procedure that can carry such a container?
results.reference: In the REGISTRATION REQUEST message, the Payload container type IE is set to 'UE policy container' as described in subclauses 5.5.1.2.2 and 5.5.1.3.2. The purpose of the UE-initiated NAS transport procedure is to provide transport of a UE policy container from the UE to the AMF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.17A, Payload container type; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.5.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The Payload container type IE is set to 'UE policy container' when the REGISTRATION REQUEST message includes a Payload container IE that carries one or more UE policy sections (e.g., UE policy delivery service container) intended for transfer to the network as part of UE policy provisioning, typically when the UE has UE policy information to send (such as UE policy classmark information or a UE-initiated response to UE policy container). The UE-initiated NAS transport procedure is used to carry such payloads (including UE policy containers, SMS, LPP messages, SOR transparent containers, or other application data) piggybacked within NAS signalling outside of a PDU session context, allowing the UE to transport this information to the network without establishing a dedicated PDU session, and is also usable during registration to convey UE policy container contents to enable ANDSP or URSP related data exchange between the UE and the network (e.g., PCF) via the AMF.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.6.3 (Generic UE configuration update / UE-initiated NAS transport procedure) and clause 9.11.3.39 (Payload container type IE)

results.question: A UE operating in single-registration mode performs an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode in 5GMM-IDLE mode. According to the coordination rules, what substates does the UE enter for 3GPP access and EMM, and what procedure does it subsequently initiate?
results.reference: The UE shall enter substates EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE and 5GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE for 3GPP access and then initiate the registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update over 3GPP access indicating "mobility registration updating" in the 5GS registration type IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.4.3, Coordination between 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM without N26 interface; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.16, EPS NAS message container
results.model_answer: The UE enters 5GMM-IDLE mode with the substate 5GMM-IDLE.EPS-NAS-ATTEMPT-ONLY-not applicable here; instead, upon successful inter-system change from S1 to N1 in idle mode, the UE enters state 5GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE for 3GPP access if it was in EMM-REGISTERED, and the corresponding EMM state remains EMM-REGISTERED. The UE subsequently initiates a Registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update (mobility registration update) to the AMF, indicating that it is performing an inter-system change from S1 to N1 mode.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.7.2a (Coordination between EMM and 5GMM) and clause 5.5.1.3 (Registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update)

results.question: What is the state of a procedure transaction when none exists, and what PTI value should be used in a command message that is not sent as a result of a received request message in such a context?
results.reference: The state is 'PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE'. In a command message not sent as a result of a received request message, the sending entity shall include the PTI value set to 'no procedure transaction identity assigned'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.2.7, PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE; TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.1, Principles of PTI handling for 5GSM procedures
results.model_answer: When no procedure transaction exists, the procedure transaction is in the PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE state. In this state, if a command message is sent that is not triggered by a received request message, the Procedure Transaction Identity value used shall be 'no procedure transaction identity assigned' (PTI = 0).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.5.1.3 (Procedure transaction inactive) and clause 9.6 (Procedure transaction identity)

results.question: In which two scenarios does a UE indicate its support for a multi-homed IPv6 PDU session, and what is a prerequisite regarding the PDU session type for these indications?
results.reference: The UE indicates support of the multi-homed IPv6 PDU session 1) during the UE-requested PDU session establishment of a PDU session of "IPv6" or "IPv4v6" PDU session type; and 2) during the UE-requested PDU session modification performed after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, for a PDU session associated with a PDN connection established when in S1 mode, if the UE is a UE operating in single-registration mode in a network supporting N26 interface, the PDU session is of "IPv6" or "IPv4v6" PDU session type, and the UE has not previously successfully performed the UE-requested PDU session modification to provide this indication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.11, Multi-homed IPv6 PDU session; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.2, 5GSM capability
results.model_answer: A UE indicates support for a multi-homed IPv6 PDU session in two scenarios: (1) during a UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure, by including the Multi-homed IPv6 PDU session support indication in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message; and (2) during the registration procedure, by including this indication within the 5GSM Core Network Capability IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message. The prerequisite in both cases is that the PDU session type must be IPv6 or IPv4v6.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.2.1 (5GSM Core Network Capability) and clause 6.4.1.2 (UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure)

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding its N1 mode capability for 3GPP access when changing its usage setting from 'data centric' to 'voice centric' and IMS voice is not available over 3GPP access only?
results.reference: If the UE's usage setting changes from 'data centric' to 'voice centric' and 'IMS voice not available' over 3GPP access only, and if the UE is only registered over 3GPP access, the UE shall disable the N1 mode capability for 3GPP access as specified in subclause 4.9.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.3, Change of UE's usage setting; TS 24.301, Clause 4.9.2, Disabling and re-enabling of UE's N1 mode capability for 3GPP access
results.model_answer: If the UE changes its usage setting from 'data centric' to 'voice centric' and IMS voice over 3GPP access is not available (i.e., voice services cannot be supported), the UE shall disable the N1 mode capability for 3GPP access, and shall handle this the same way as when 'the UE's usage setting is voice centric and the UE's 5GMM cause value is #62' — i.e., it shall follow the actions specified for a UE that cannot support N1 mode for 3GPP access due to voice service unavailability, including locally releasing the N1 NAS signalling connection and, if applicable, disabling the N1 mode capability for 3GPP access until switched off, USIM is removed, or the UE is unable to obtain normal service.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.9.2 (N1 mode capability for 3GPP access)

results.question: For which PDU session types is the 'Maximum number of supported packet filters' IE included in the message after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, and what is a key characteristic of the UE's operation mode and network interface in this scenario?
results.reference: The 'Maximum number of supported packet filters' IE shall be included in the message for a PDN connection established when in S1 mode, after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, if the UE is a UE operating in single-registration mode in a network supporting N26 interface, the PDU session type is "IPv4", "IPv6", "IPv4v6" or "Ethernet", and the UE can support more than 16 packet filters for this PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.4, Maximum number of supported packet filters; TS 24.301, Clause 4.8.2.2, Single-registration mode with N26 interface
results.model_answer: The 'Maximum number of supported packet filters' IE is included in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message only for PDU sessions of IP type (IPv4, IPv6, or IPv4v6) after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode. A key characteristic of this scenario is that the UE operates in single-registration mode and has moved from E-UTRA connected to EPC (S1 mode) to NR connected to 5GCN (N1 mode), requiring the UE to indicate its supported packet filter capability to the network since this information was not previously exchanged under EPS.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.2.3 (PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST) and clause 6.1.2 (Interactions between EMM and 5GMM)

results.question: What message does a UE acting as a relay send to initiate the remote UE report procedure, and what must the UE do if timer T3586 expires for the first time after sending this message?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure by creating and sending a REMOTE UE REPORT message. If timer T3586 expires for the first time, the UE shall resend the REMOTE UE REPORT message and shall reset and restart timer T3586.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.2, Remote UE report procedure initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.4, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The relay UE sends a REMOTE UE REPORT message to initiate the remote UE report procedure. If timer T3586 expires for the first time after sending this message, the relay UE shall resend the REMOTE UE REPORT message and restart timer T3586.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.4 (Remote UE report procedure), including sub-clause on abnormal cases in the UE (T3586 expiry handling).

results.question: What message does the UE send to the AMF after receiving an EAP-request/AKA'-challenge message and successfully authenticating the network, and what does the AMF do upon receiving that message?
results.reference: The UE sends an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message containing an EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message. Upon receipt of the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message, the AMF shall stop timer T3560.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.3, UE successfully authenticates network; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.3, EAP message reliable transport procedure accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE sends an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message containing an EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message to the AMF. Upon receiving this message, the AMF shall send it to the AUSF, which verifies the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge and, if successful, proceeds to complete the EAP-AKA' authentication procedure (typically resulting in an EAP-success message being sent to the UE via the AMF, encapsulated in a NAS message such as the SECURITY MODE COMMAND).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.2.2 (EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure - EAP-AKA')

results.question: What is the fundamental difference in context management between a UE operating in single-registration mode and one operating in dual-registration mode when both 5GMM and EMM are enabled?
results.reference: If both 5GMM and EMM are enabled, a UE operating in single-registration mode shall maintain one common registration for 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM. In contrast, a UE operating in the dual-registration mode shall maintain independent contexts for 5GMM and EMM, which includes independent lists of equivalent PLMNs.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.4.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 4.8.3, Dual-registration mode
results.model_answer: In single-registration mode, the UE maintains a single common registration for both 5GMM and EMM, using a shared/mapped security and mobility context across 3GPP access to N1 mode and S1 mode, with only one active MM state (either registered in 5GMM or EMM at a time via mapped context, coordinated through interworking procedures). In dual-registration mode, the UE maintains independent 5GMM and EMM contexts, performing separate, independent registrations with the network in N1 mode and S1 mode, each with its own security context, without requiring context mapping or coordination between the two registration states.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 4.8 (Coexistence of 5GS and EPS: single-registration mode and dual-registration mode)

results.question: What action does the AMF take if timer T3560 expires for the first time during an EAP-based authentication procedure, and what is the consequence if it expires for the fifth time?
results.reference: On the first expiry of timer T3560, the AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and shall reset and start timer T3560. On the fifth expiry of timer T3560, the AMF shall abort the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure and any ongoing 5GMM specific procedure, and release the N1 NAS signalling connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: If timer T3560 expires for the first time, the AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and shall reset and restart timer T3560. This retransmission is performed up to five times. If timer T3560 expires for the fifth time (i.e., after the fifth retransmission), the AMF shall abort the authentication procedure, and any ongoing 5GMM procedure shall be aborted; the AMF may release the NAS signalling connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.4 (Abnormal cases on the network side, EAP-based authentication - T3560 expiry handling)

results.question: Which message does the AMF send to reject a service request procedure, and which message does it send to reject a registration procedure?
results.reference: To reject a service request procedure, the AMF sends the SERVICE REJECT message to the UE. To reject a registration procedure, the AMF sends the REGISTRATION REJECT message to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.18.1, Message definition; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.9.1, Message definition
results.model_answer: For a rejected Service Request procedure, the AMF sends a SERVICE REJECT message. For a rejected Registration procedure, the AMF sends a REGISTRATION REJECT message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 5.5.1.2.5 (Registration reject) and 5.6.1.5 (Service reject)

results.question: What PTI value should be included in a command message sent by the network when initiating a procedure transaction towards the UE, and what is the corresponding state of the procedure transaction in the network at that moment?
results.reference: The sending entity shall include in the command message the PTI value set to 'no procedure transaction identity assigned'. The corresponding state in the network is 'PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING', as the network has initiated a procedure transaction towards the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.1, Principles of PTI handling for 5GSM procedures; TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.3.7, PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING
results.model_answer: The network shall include a PTI value that is not '0' or 'no assigned PTI value' (i.e., a newly assigned, unused PTI value) in the command message when initiating a procedure transaction towards the UE. At that moment, the corresponding procedure transaction in the network is in state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE, and upon sending the command message it transitions to PTI PENDING.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.2.2 (5GSM procedure transaction states) and clause 6.3.1 (procedure transaction identity)

results.question: What is included in the NSAG information that the network may send, and what condition must the UE meet to potentially receive it?
results.reference: NSAG information includes a list of NSAG IDs each associated with a list of S-NSSAIs, an NSAG area containing a list of TAIs, and a priority value. The network may include this IE if the UE has set the NSAG bit to 'NSAG supported' in the 5GMM capability IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.6.2.6, Provision of NSAG information to lower layers; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.51, NSAG information
results.model_answer: The NSAG information (Network Slice Area Group information) that the network may send to the UE includes: the NSAG ID, the associated S-NSSAI(s), and the list of tracking areas (TAs) belonging to that NSAG. The network may send this information in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message (or via UE configuration update procedure) provided the UE has indicated support for Network Slice-Specific Area of Validity and the network supports and decides to provide NSAG information for the current PLMN/tracking area.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.4 and 9.11.3.85 (NSAG Information IE)

results.question: What triggers the UE to initiate the authentication and key agreement procedure for a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay, and what is the first action the UE must take as part of that initiation?
